title: The Great Game
summary: The Great Game is the name for the rivalry between Britain and Russia for influence in Central Asia and neighbouring lands. The phrase is credited to Arthur Conolly, who used it in 1840, though historian Malcolm Yapp argues the rivalry sense came later. The Anglo-Russian Convention of August 1907 formally ended the contest.

uncertainty.note: Sources give no sharp start: 'early nineteenth century' (Yapp). The id year 1830 is only a lookup key. End: Anglo-Russian Convention, August 1907.
